items.text: Verified release migration: src/sh/release.sh removed; src/kash/release.kash owns operator preflight, signed staging, GitHub draft creation/upload/verification/publish, and npm retry from immutable tagged assets. E404-only publication semantics and accepted/pending status 3 are preserved. Thin src/kash/release-publish.kash accepts --repo and --notes-file via parse-args; direct entry expects prebuilt dist assets. Kamefile release builds assets then invokes the function with [tty: :true foreground: :true]. No network publication was attempted. Native terminal-authority implementation: eval.Context.TerminalAuthority in lang/eval/terminal.go and host/posix/terminal.go; required handoff without a terminal fails HOST_FAIL, busy handoff EXPR_INVALID. Restore remembers the actual previous terminal foreground process group, not the Kame group. Restore errors fail otherwise-successful completions without replacing child failures. docs/spec/051 records limitations: Kash recipe bodies only, one foreground stage due to separate cancellation groups, and environment authority unimplemented. Homebrew template src/kash/templates/kame.rb and etc/kame.rb install a relative kash->kame link and smoke-test it. npm/Scoop intentionally remain kame-only by user choice. Verification: 84 related shell suites passed; go vet ./..., go test ./..., compiled CLI suite with KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY and KAME_NATIVE_FORMAT_TEST_BINARY passed; darwin and wasip1 cross-builds passed. Final post-format release suites passed T015-06 44/44 and T015-04 7/7. Implementation gotchas: wildcard returns session-relative paths even under with :cwd, so release uses basenames and rejoins with an explicit directory before lstat/read/upload. Kash def returns status only; use expression-bodied functions for values. Stage setups precede command head (e.g. :tty :true npm ...). Raw Kash quoted command args interpolate ${name}; Kame expression strings use @{name}. Repeated --allow-env=NAME is necessary because the current CLI does not split comma-separated lists.
items.title: Kash release migration

items.text: Interactive Kash REPL phase 1 implemented per docs/spec/052-kash-interactive.md: `kash` on a TTY, `kash -i`, and `kame do run -i`. Session.AppendKash grows the live session incrementally without replay; entries are source parts named <kash:N>; failures end only the entry; SIGINT cancels only the current entry. Verified by `go test ./...` and native cmd/kame tests (TestNativeInteractiveKashSession).
golang.org/x/term v0.33.0 returns io.EOF for both Ctrl-C and Ctrl-D and keeps the triggering bytes buffered, so recreate Terminal after an interrupt; also guard SetSize against 0x0 pty sizes.
Runtime diagnostics locate spans through eval SourceParts and clamp to the last part, so text appended to a compiled session must register its own SourcePart (AddSourcePart) for correct locations.

Legacy memory/all learnings lacked an identity, which memo agent bind requires. `memo meta get` output includes a '# ID' header line, so parse the value (e.g. awk '/^uuid: /{print $2}') before reusing it; identities cannot be changed or removed via the CLI once set.

Known later-phase gaps: no terminal handoff to children (spec 051 handoff unimplemented), no cd/export, and background & work is joined at session end. Windows cmd/kame build fails in host/posix/locks.go (pre-existing).

Kash REPL phase 2 verified: interactive terminal sessions hand the controlling terminal to foreground statement graphs (spec docs/spec/052-kash-interactive.md, 'Terminal handoff'), via eval.Program.Terminal -> payload 'terminal' -> host.ProcessRequest.Terminal -> host/posix/terminal.go terminalHandoff in both topology.go and posix.go Start paths. REPL-level cd, export, unset (cmd/kame/repl_shell.go) change session directory (program.Program.SetDirectory; default grants follow cwd, explicit grants never) and child environment (Program.SetEnvironment). Linux pty regression test: cmd/kame/repl_terminal_linux_test.go.

host/posix ownedProcess.wait SIGKILLs the leader's whole process group when the leader is reaped, so pipeline stages must keep separate process groups; terminal handoff therefore makes only one stage foreground (last stage writing to the terminal, else first stage reading it).
Go SysProcAttr.Foreground takes Ctty as a PARENT descriptor number (unlike Setctty, which takes a child fd) and calls tcsetpgrp in the child before exec, avoiding the read-before-handoff race.
Lines typed ahead while a command runs in cooked mode arrive with Enter translated to '\n' (ICRNL); golang.org/x/term only accepts '\r', so the REPL input wrapper maps '\n' to '\r'.

Kame's live progress dashboard and OSC 9;4 taskbar draw on the terminal during long commands and corrupt full-screen programs; interactive sessions disable them (dashboardLive=false, taskbarEnabled=false).
Package program must stay host-neutral: importing kame/host/posix breaks the wasip1 build (cmd/kame-wasm); verify with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build ./cmd/kame-wasm.

Interactive Kash support is documented in docs/spec/052-kash-interactive.md: startup-file precedence is $KASH_INIT, then $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/kash/init.kash, then ~/.config/kash/init.kash; empty KASH_INIT disables startup. Prompts use session function kash-prompt and fall back to the default on failure; Tab completion covers bindings, functions after (, session commands/keywords/PATH executables in command position, cd directories, and paths otherwise. Job control remains a non-goal. Implementation is in src/go/kame/cmd/kame/repl.go and repl_complete.go, and lang/eval/interactive.go. Interactive entries now accept comments, and Ctrl-C preserves subsequently typed bytes. Native CLI tests require KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY; TestHelpAndVersion requires a debug artifactMode build, and interactive tests set KASH_INIT= to isolate from user startup files. Verified go test ./... and the full native cmd/kame suite pass.
items.title: Interactive Kash implementation and testing notes

items.text: Kame lexical lambdas and placeholder sections now bind missing declared parameters to nil; only too many arguments are EXPR_INVALID. Collection callbacks map, flatmap, filter, and filter-out pass the item alone to unary callables and (item, zero-based position) to callables declaring two or more parameters, with further parameters nil. Arity diagnostics for lexical functions point at the authored parameter list, including brackets. Verified with go test ./... and the T007-02 and T014-01 shell suites.
items.title: Kame dynamic arity and indexed collection callbacks

items.text: Verified project facts: The interactive Kash terminal editor uses github.com/reeflective/readline v1.3.0 rather than golang.org/x/term, adding only rivo/uniseg. Its implementation is in src/go/kame/cmd/kame/repl_editor.go, repl_complete.go, lang/script/kash_tokens.go, and lang/eval/interactive.go; completionsAt returns tagged/described candidates, KashTokens is a tolerant highlighting lexer, and InteractiveNames returns []InteractiveName with Callable/Detail. docs/spec/052-kash-interactive.md describes line editing and highlighting; completion is a grouped menu using menu-complete-display-prefix, and history stores multiline entries with trailing-backslash continuation lines. Verified gotchas: readline renders on os.Stdout, so swap os.Stdout to stderr when stdout is not a terminal. Disable cursor-position-probe when TERM is dumb/empty to avoid hangs; with a real TERM, pty tests must answer ESC[6n with ESC[1;1R. Default Tab completion inserts the first candidate without listing unless menu-complete-display-prefix is set. Tab at line start must insert a tab for block bodies. Readline echoes Ctrl-C itself. Pseudo-terminal tests must wait until the editor is reading (last ESC[?25h with nothing after) before Ctrl-D, or cooked tty consumes EOF. Release targets are linux and darwin (amd64/arm64) and build; windows/BSD cmd/kame builds already fail independently in host/posix. lang/script tests are registered in generated lang/script/test/go_tests_test.go as sorted t.Run lines.
items.title: Kash REPL moved to reeflective/readline with completion menu and highlighting

Native CLI regression tests in src/go/kame/cmd/kame, including interactive Kash/pseudo-terminal tests, silently skip unless KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY is set to an absolute path of a built binary. Run `go build -o /tmp/kame-native ./cmd/kame && KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY=/tmp/kame-native go test ./cmd/kame/`; a plain go test pass does not verify them.
2. Shell conformance tests are in tests/T*.sh and run directly with `bash tests/NAME.sh`; scripts build the binary via lib-bootstrap.sh.
3. Commit messages follow `[Update] scope[, scope]: Summary` followed by a prose body; keep unrelated language changes in separate commits from feature work.
4. Interactive Kash (docs/spec/052-kash-interactive.md) uses github.com/reeflective/readline in cmd/kame/repl_editor.go, with highlighting driven by lang/script/kash_tokens.go. Keep docs/ref-kash.md and docs/skills/kame/ref/kash.md synchronized with spec 052.

items.text: Native CLI/pty tests in src/go/kame/cmd/kame are skipped unless KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY is set to an absolute path of a built kame binary; plain go test can pass while skipping them. To run them, build with `go build -o /tmp/kame-x ./cmd/kame` and run `KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY=/tmp/kame-x go test ./cmd/kame -run 'NativeInteractive|NativeRecipeTerminal'`.
TestHelpAndVersion fails against a plain `go build` binary because buildMode is "development"; this failure is expected and is not a regression.

Interactive `&` graphs attach to the terminal in the background. capture() sets the eval Context field TerminalBackground when e.Async and p.Terminal are true, and the `terminalBackground` payload key sets host ProcessRequest.TerminalBackground. After evaluation, job status is derived from its last failed `&` graph (`asyncStatus`).

The interactive-session `--timeout` exit stopped background jobs even before `s.cancelJobs()` was added to that path; testing a binary built without that fix confirmed the suspected join hang was not real.
On `fg`, host running.resume treats errTerminalBusy as “continue in background”, so a job with multiple terminal-attached graphs resumes all of them.

Kash interactive sessions support an optional right prompt through the session function kash-rprompt, called after kash-prompt with the same [status: dir: name: jobs:] record. Its string result is passed to reeflective/readline Prompt.Right (editorReader.right in src/go/kame/cmd/kame/repl_editor.go); it renders at the right edge of the entry last line and is omitted when there is no room. Failures emit a <kash-rprompt> diagnostic and show no right prompt. Both prompt calls share replSession.callPrompt in repl.go. Specification docs/spec/052-kash-interactive.md covers this in the Prompt section, non-goals, and conformance row; TestNativeInteractiveKashRightPrompt tests it. Separately, TestHelpAndVersion fails with a native CLI binary built by plain go build because without release ldflags buildMode is development; that failure is expected for an ad-hoc binary.

For native CLI test runs, build the binary with -ldflags "-X main.artifactMode=debug" before setting KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY; an ordinary go build leaves artifactMode=development and makes TestHelpAndVersion fail its accepted-mode check. The canonical Kamefile debug target uses this ldflag.

PTY tests of terminalSession must isolate the redraw produced after a fresh clear-screen marker (\x1b[H\x1b[2J) when asserting current interactive layout after sending multiple keys. Raw PTY output accumulates intermediate redraws, so searching all bytes after key input can falsely find transient states before input reaches its final overlap/layout condition. Require a completed redraw suffix before inspecting that segment. Verified in TestNativeInteractiveKashRightPromptUnicodeEditing; repeated five times successfully.
Added focused guidance for interpreting accumulated PTY redraw output in interactive layout tests.

When filtering or scoping Kash readline history, invalidate the editor’s per-source undo cache as well as filtering/removing history sources: reeflective/readline v1.3.0 can serve cached recalled text without Source.GetLine, and Sources.Delete leaves cached undo lines. Use public Walk/Revert at submission, scope-change, and expiration boundaries while preserving the current buffer and cursor.

items.text: When running native CLI regression tests for cmd/kame, build the test binary with artifactMode set to debug, release, or sanitize via -ldflags (for example, -ldflags "-X main.artifactMode=debug") and set KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY to its absolute path. A plain go build leaves buildMode=development and causes TestHelpAndVersion to fail even when focused tests pass.

For native CLI tests, build the binary supplied through KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY with -ldflags "-X main.artifactMode=debug" (as the Kamefile does); a plain go build binary causes TestHelpAndVersion to fail with "unexpected compiled build/runtime". This extends the existing run-native-cli-tests guidance.

Kash mode selection uses the argv[0] basename exactly "kash" (or "-kash"); a profiling symlink with another basename, such as "kashp", silently selects kame mode. To profile the Kash entry point, use a directory containing a symlink named kash.

Kash profiling can avoid repository edits by using go build -overlay overlay.json to inject a runtime/pprof or runtime/trace hook file into cmd/kame and patch dispatch.go to call it before os.Exit. Linux perf was unavailable on the measured machine because perf_event_paranoid=2.

The development machine was heavily loaded during the 2026-11-17 Kash performance session (load average about 20 on 4 cores); benchmark comparisons should use child CPU time from getrusage rather than wall time to reduce load-related noise.

In the Go runtime, core.Value is 272 bytes. mem.System.Free is a no-op on Go builds, but Value.Free zeroes list elements in place; therefore list and record backing aliases require reference counting. The implemented core.Value.Shared / SharedStorage, Share, Unshare, and CloneOwned APIs provide that ownership handling. Engine subscribers must receive CloneOwned values, as enforced by the TestSubscribersOwnCoalescedBatchLists contract.

The 2026-11-17 Kash performance session implemented host/posix FileSignature using crypto/sha256 with a process-wide stat-keyed digest memo and a 2-second racy window; OutputPassthrough lets eligible foreground direct-session statement graphs inherit file descriptors 1 and 2 (spec 042 section 2 updated); shared list/record backing support; memoized operation version signatures; and source-part observation names. Spec 026 gained a "File content signatures" section.

Kash keystroke latency: TestNativeInteractiveKashKeystrokeLatency compares kash with bash on the same PTY. Verified causes of lag: per-key highlighter round trips to the session goroutine (blocked ~10ms by job ticks) and a per-entry PATH stat scan (~16ms first key); fixed by a per-entry highlight snapshot set in replSession.read and a mtime-keyed PATH listing cache. Readline's enable-bracketed-paste defaults to false; kash now enables it. Remaining gap: typeahead bursts (~35ms/210 keys vs bash <1ms) because reeflective readline redraws once per key; fixing needs a readline patch or replacement (user prefers replacement over more patches, but vi mode is required). Also: TestHelpAndVersion needs a binary built with -ldflags '-X main.artifactMode=debug'.

readline fork: github.com/sebastien/readline (fork of reeflective/readline) holds one branch per upstream PR (perf/match-bind, perf/coalesce-redraw, perf/probe-once-per-line, perf/lazy-init) and a 'kame' integration branch = upstream master + unmerged patches. Upstream #118 already contains Kame's old cursor-probe-swallow patch. Kame's vendored probe-once-per-line patch has a bug: Ctrl-C at a real-terminal prompt loses the ^C echo (hidden in kame tests because TERM=dumb disables the probe); fixed in the fork via Engine.AcceptLineEcho. Profiling kash bursts showed keymap.matchBind sorting all binds per key byte (~60us/key); fixed in perf/match-bind. With the kame branch: burst 210 keys ~2ms (bash 0.6ms), typing ~100us/key. Profiling trick: inject a pprof init file with go build -overlay; perf is blocked by perf_event_paranoid=2.

readline now comes from git-deps: .gitdeps pins deps/readline (git@github.com:sebastien/readline.git, branch kame); deps/readline is gitignored and src/go/third_party/readline is a symlink to ../../../deps/readline, so go.mod's replace path is unchanged. Run 'git-deps checkout --missing' after cloning. CI workflows fetch .gitdeps entries over HTTPS in a 'Fetch dependencies' step (pattern from appenv). Upstream PRs: reeflective/readline#125 (match-bind), #126 (coalesce-redraw), #127 (probe-once-per-line + ^C echo fix), #128 (lazy-init). To update: rebuild the fork's kame branch from master + unmerged perf/* branches, push, then git-deps update deps/readline && git-deps save.

Primary coding agent for the Kame repository: the Go runtime and CLI, the Kame and Kash languages, and the specifications under docs/spec. Works spec-first, verifies with the Go suites and native CLI tests, and records verified project knowledge through memo.

operations.text:
When a static Kash check needs bindings or captures from earlier source fragments, use syntax-only parsing during fragment discovery and validate the composed unit before effects. Test both the valid cross-fragment reference and rejection before effects through the native and WASM entry points, since their preflight paths can differ.

When changing Kame source loaders, evaluate a conditional during composition only if it selects included sources at the loader's scope. Leave other conditionals for declaration registration so they retain its evaluation authority. A declaration-local include stays with its enclosing block and is registered in each reached iteration scope even if the source read is shared. Test declaration-phase discovery, ordinary conditional includes, and two iterations that include the same file but use different bindings through the native and WASM paths when supported. When testing list contributions across declaration-local includes, read the same list in a condition between includes and in a recipe registered before the later contribution. This checks both the reached prefix during registration and the final list the recipe consumes.

Test include path validation separately from the source origin. An inline source has no base for a relative include, but it can include an absolute or home-relative path. Pair those successful inline cases with an inline relative rejection, and separately check that an invalid included Kash module reports DEF_INVALID before effects.

When testing conditional include selection, place the authored source in a different directory from the evaluation cwd. Under CLI `-C`, verify that a relative path expression in a condition uses the effective working directory while the selected relative include still resolves beside its authoring file.

When an early include condition uses `files`, exercise the read-grant check and verify that its membership observation reaches both registration and watch. Add a conflicting declared output and assert overlap at the authored discovery span. Then start watch with a selected include missing and change only discovery membership to make another branch viable. The build should recover without editing the source, and ordinary content reads and effects should still be rejected in conditions.

report.summary: Verify both registration-time and recipe-time views of declaration-local contributions.

drive-closed-pipe-tests-until-closure.text:
When testing a callable stage whose downstream reader exits, send bounded chunks one at a time after each acknowledgement until the host reports closure or the test deadline expires. A pipe can accept an initial write while the reader is exiting. After closure, check the stage cancellation and final graph outcome.

Also test a generator that keeps yielding without writing and a generator blocked in a confirmed-started subprocess or stdin read. Schedule the stdout closure watch independently so it can wake a waiting stage. Cancel an active subprocess request and await its terminal acknowledgement before unwinding. Close borrowed readers through their existing ownership path. On native and WASM, assert aggregate success, cancelled stage outcome, and cleanup separately. Preserve structured completions for configured and topology process requests so the WASM success shortcut cannot discard per-stage outcomes.

Test a consumer that closes stdin and stays alive until the generator cleans up. The Node host can detect reader closure by opening the private FIFO with O_WRONLY | O_NONBLOCK and checking for ENXIO, without writing probe bytes or changing endpoint flags. Keep names only for watched FIFOs. Remove their private directory when the graph joins or launch fails, and check for leftovers after the test.
drive-closed-pipe-tests-until-closure.title: Test downstream closure while a callable writes, yields, or waits

isolate-declaration-captures-in-freshnes.text: When testing freshness for rules created in declaration blocks, keep the recipe source, target, and ordinary inputs fixed across builds. Change only an input to a declaration-time binding and assert that the rebuilt artifact reflects the new captured value. This exercises the declaration scope signature without relying on cache invalidation from a changed recipe or target.
isolate-declaration-captures-in-freshnes.title: Isolate declaration captures in rule freshness tests

preserve-callable-ownership-in-process-o.text:
Keep returned lexical closures in evaluator-owned process outcomes, outside process wire metadata and engine-published values. Core Clone and CloneOwned copy value storage without retaining callable wrappers. Use the evaluator's callable borrowing and release helpers when copying or freeing an outcome, and retain async closure snapshots to the end of their script group. Verify the returned closure still works in a fresh scope after capture, command-list selection, and repeated waits.

When changing Kash let or set with returned closures, test a binding that owns a closure capturing its descendant scope, including container values and replacement. In the lifetime test, retain an external callable borrow, release the initial scope owners, and verify both scopes stay reachable. Release the last borrow and verify that both scopes clear. Separately invoke a returned callable after rebinding and host suspension.
preserve-callable-ownership-in-process-o.title: Preserve callable ownership across outcomes and bindings

pty-redraw-assertions.text: When a PTY test asserts the editor's current layout after multiple keys, inspect only a completed redraw beginning at the fresh clear-screen marker (\x1b[H\x1b[2J), not all output accumulated since the keys were sent; intermediate redraws can represent transient input states and cause false failures.
pty-redraw-assertions.title: Assert fresh PTY redraws

register-host-process-before-async-launc.text: In the Node WASM host, register the process group under its instance and request ID before the launch path can yield. Cancellation and signal handlers should await group readiness. Resolve readiness on launch failure or completion without a child so control requests can finish. Exercise immediate control after start and check that a second job remains unaffected.
register-host-process-before-async-launc.title: Register process requests before asynchronous launch

run-native-cli-tests.text: When verifying changes to the native CLI or interactive Kash tests, build the CLI and set KAME_NATIVE_CLI_TEST_BINARY to its absolute path before running the package tests; otherwise those tests silently skip and a passing plain `go test` is incomplete.
run-native-cli-tests.title: Run native CLI tests explicitly

test-absent-and-invalid-host-edge-teleme.text: When changing process graph telemetry, exercise both absence and malformed data at the WASM host completion boundary. Remove optional edge metrics and verify unavailable measurements with null counters. Then corrupt a row, counter, or measurement kind and verify that HOST_FAIL reaches the caller even through an inspected process outcome. Keep the ordinary terminal graph parity checks alongside these protocol tests.
test-absent-and-invalid-host-edge-teleme.title: Test absent and malformed host edge telemetry separately

validate-composed-lexical-context.text:
When a static Kash check needs bindings or captures from earlier source fragments, use syntax-only parsing during fragment discovery and validate the composed unit before effects. Test both the valid cross-fragment reference and rejection before effects through the native and WASM entry points, since their preflight paths can differ.

When changing Kame source loaders, evaluate a conditional during composition only if it selects included sources at the loader's scope. Leave other conditionals for declaration registration so they retain its evaluation authority. A declaration-local include stays with its enclosing block and is registered in each reached iteration scope even if the source read is shared. Test declaration-phase discovery, ordinary conditional includes, and two iterations that include the same file but use different bindings through the native and WASM paths when supported. When testing list contributions across declaration-local includes, read the same list in a condition between includes and in a recipe registered before the later contribution. This checks both the reached prefix during registration and the final list the recipe consumes.

Test include path validation separately from the source origin. An inline source has no base for a relative include, but it can include an absolute or home-relative path. Pair those successful inline cases with an inline relative rejection, and separately check that an invalid included Kash module reports DEF_INVALID before effects.

When testing conditional include selection, place the authored source in a different directory from the evaluation cwd. Under CLI `-C`, verify that a relative path expression in a condition uses the effective working directory while the selected relative include still resolves beside its authoring file.

When an early include condition uses `files`, exercise the read-grant check and verify that its membership observation reaches both registration and watch. Add a conflicting declared output and assert overlap at the authored discovery span. Then start watch with a selected include missing and change only discovery membership to make another branch viable. The build should recover without editing the source, and ordinary content reads and effects should still be rejected in conditions.
validate-composed-lexical-context.title: Preserve evaluation context during source composition

verify-borrowed-stdin-handoff-and-cancel.text:
When changing callable stdin, test both handoff directions between a subprocess and a framed reader. Check the exact unread tail, including when the delimiter arrives after multiple transport chunks. Exercise cancellation with a FIFO whose writer stays open: after a subprocess consumes one byte, let a sibling fail while the callable waits for a record. Require the reader and callable cleanup to finish before closing the writer. Close the active reader before joining the callable.

In the Node host, keep the inherited pipe descriptor free from eager Socket reads. Opening a Socket early can prefetch bytes the subprocess should receive. When Node needs a nonblocking FIFO reader, use an independent descriptor and lend the blocking descriptor to subprocesses. On Go, spawn can make the shared descriptor blocking; poll with a bounded wait before a framed read so cancellation can still wake it. Verify nested subprocess inheritance and transfers larger than the pipe buffer on both hosts.
verify-borrowed-stdin-handoff-and-cancel.title: Preserve callable stdin descriptor handoff

verify-changed-inputs-through-indirect-c.text: When testing preparation of the changed-inputs snapshot, put its only reference in an imported helper invoked inside an async capture. A direct recipe reference can cause the snapshot to be prepared even if indirect consumers are missed. Verify a first build, a changed normal input, and a forced build with no content changes.
verify-changed-inputs-through-indirect-c.title: Test changed-inputs through an imported helper

verify-command-probes-in-kash-loop-fixtu.text: When migrating a Kash loop fixture whose condition used to run a command, verify the new header inspects an explicit process outcome such as `while $?(./probe).ok`. A legacy `while ./probe` still parses as a truthy path and can hang the harness. Use an external timeout around the CLI invocation and assert the probe ran and the loop terminated.
verify-command-probes-in-kash-loop-fixtu.title: Verify command probes in migrated Kash loop fixtures

verify-deliberate-exit-at-sync-capture-b.text:
When changing deliberate exit handling in synchronous Kash captures, exercise both text capture and inspected outcomes. Have a command-list member emit a prefix, a later member exit after registering a defer that emits a second marker, and a skipped member carry a forbidden marker. Assert that the capture retains the prefix and cleanup bytes in order, reports the appropriate text or status, and lets the caller emit a continuation marker. Consume the exit at the synchronous capture unit boundary after cleanup.

Inspect a direct pipeline and a pipeline reached in a command list to verify that exit handling preserves per-stage status and terminal graph metadata. Also test an ordinary deferred failure that remains inspectable and a later cleanup CAP_DENIED after an ordinary primary failure. The combined denial must still stop the caller, leave stdout empty, and retain both diagnostic codes.
verify-deliberate-exit-at-sync-capture-b.title: Verify deliberate exit at the synchronous capture boundary

verify-expected-tools-besides-host-parit.text: When changing tool inspection, exercise both global do tools and dependency-scoped do tools check. Assert expected tool names and missing-tool diagnostics in addition to comparing native and WASM output: parity can pass when both omit tools. Include a default Kash body without shell metadata and an explicit x/ command head. Verify the name is reported without its namespace and that a missing tool on a reached dependency carries the selected target stack.
verify-expected-tools-besides-host-parit.title: Check expected tools in both inspection modes

verify-fairness-with-one-ready-slot.text: When changing engine dispatch, keep Ready and Step on the same resource-key rotation. Exercise a one-slot dispatch while a generator keeps becoming ready and another node must complete its parent graph. A scheduler that always picks the first ready key can keep the generator running and starve completion and cleanup.
verify-fairness-with-one-ready-slot.title: Verify engine fairness with one ready slot

verify-inherited-environment-removal.text: When changing process environment setup, seed a variable in the parent test environment, remove it in Kash, and assert its absence inside an external child on both the native and WASM hosts. The evaluator can report the variable as absent while a backend still inherits the original value.
verify-inherited-environment-removal.title: Verify environment removals in the launched child

verify-missing-module-source-observation.text: When changing authored module lookup, verify what happens when a previously missing candidate appears and when an existing source changes. A missing candidate is a valid source-host completion and must be observed for proof revalidation. For a conditional include, select a branch to load its source, switch away, and edit the now-inactive file. Verify that watch stays idle during the edit and reads the edited file when the branch is selected again. This sequence exercises previously retained source state. For an imported declaration-time constructor, add an unrelated missing import to the fixture and verify registration succeeds while still tracking the sources the constructor reaches transitively. An eager static edge to the missing import would block registration. Keep these checks on the compiler source-loading path so they do not depend on general read grants.
verify-missing-module-source-observation.title: Verify module watch dependencies for missing and inactive sources

verify-prebuilt-harness-artifact-inputs.text: When a harness fixture uses additional build or release artifacts, check every Kamefile task that runs it with `KAME_TEST_PREBUILT`. The harness skips its prebuild in that mode, so a populated local `dist` can hide missing task prerequisites. Compare the fixture's artifact inputs with each caller's declared dependencies, and verify the task's input plan or run it in a clean workspace.
verify-prebuilt-harness-artifact-inputs.title: Verify artifact prerequisites for prebuilt harness runs

verify-process-environment-freshness.text:
Use the primary build invocation when proving recipe freshness. Explicit do run recipe execution requests forced runs and cannot establish a warm cache hit. A primary build with explicit grants can still take the unified runner path. If that fixture needs to prove cache reuse without data input, supply terminal stdin through a PTY so an inherited nonterminal descriptor does not become an opaque input. Count actual recipe executions as well as checking output, since identical output can come from either a cache hit or a needless rerun. To prove downstream invalidation, choose an upstream edit that changes the bytes of the intermediate artifact and verify that the consumer reruns. A comment-only C edit may rerun compilation while leaving object bytes unchanged and allowing the link step to reuse its result.

When testing process environment freshness, first vary ambient values hidden by unit or stage overrides and removals and check that the build is reused. Then change a value inherited by the child and check that the build reruns.
verify-process-environment-freshness.title: Verify recipe reuse and reruns through primary builds

verify-quiescence-after-latest-watch-idl.text: Before asserting that a watch log stays unchanged, parse only complete JSON lines and wait until the latest event is watch-idle for at least the required cycle. Also verify the expected output and that the watcher is alive. An earlier idle event can coexist with visible writes from an active later cycle. Read the log through a separate handle so the test does not move the writer's file offset.
verify-quiescence-after-latest-watch-idl.title: Wait for the latest watch cycle before asserting quiescence

verify-service-restart-readiness-per-gen.text: When testing whether a dependent resumes after a service health restart, trigger the first health failure only after the dependent has started. If readiness is represented by a filesystem marker, retire the old marker before reporting failure and have the replacement publish its own readiness. Verify that the dependent starts again after replacement readiness. A stale marker can let the readiness probe succeed before the replacement process starts.
verify-service-restart-readiness-per-gen.title: Test readiness for each service generation

verify-standalone-wasm-process-evaluatio.text:
When changing WASM evaluation of process expressions, exercise KameProgram.evaluate directly. The standalone evaluator needs the shared host tool-resolution request and portable capture default even when no CLI session is compiled. Test captured stdout, inspected exit status, a lazily evaluated definition, caller cwd, missing-tool fallback, and denial without run grants.

When running `tests/wasm/test-memory-reuse.mjs` against a freshly built module, set `KAME_WASM` to that module's path. The script selects the binary from that variable or falls back to `build/wasm/kame.wasm`. Positional arguments have no effect on binary selection.

When changing source-backed evaluation in the JavaScript API, compile with an absolute source name and test `KameProgram.evaluate` against a relative authored import. Vary the evaluation cwd independently, verify the imported module retains its own file provenance, and check that a general read of the same file is denied when compile grants only scoped source access. A separately parsed evaluation AST needs the compiled program’s lexical source origin alongside its expression diagnostic location.
verify-standalone-wasm-process-evaluatio.title: Verify process evaluation through the standalone WASM API

verify-suspended-declaration-registratio.text: When changing declaration work that can suspend on a forwarded host request, drive prepare, request, and completion separately. Check that suspension and failure leave no partial program installed. Count repeated requests during replay, and verify that an unsuccessful registration retains the observations needed for watch to recover.
verify-suspended-declaration-registratio.title: Verify declaration registration across forwarded completions

A comment-only C edit may rerun compilation while leaving object bytes unchanged and allowing the link step to reuse its result.

When testing process environment freshness, first vary ambient values hidden by unit or stage overrides and removals and check that the build is reused. Then change a value inherited by the child and check that the build reruns.
verify-process-environment-freshness.title: Verify recipe reuse and reruns through primary builds

verify-quiescence-after-latest-watch-idl.text: Before asserting that a watch log stays unchanged, parse only complete JSON lines and wait until the latest event is watch-idle for at least the required cycle. Also verify the expected output and that the watcher is alive. An earlier idle event can coexist with visible writes from an active later cycle. Read the log through a separate handle so the test does not move the writer's file offset.
verify-quiescence-after-latest-watch-idl.title: Wait for the latest watch cycle before asserting quiescence

verify-service-restart-readiness-per-gen.text: When testing whether a dependent resumes after a service health restart, trigger the first health failure only after the dependent has started. If readiness is represented by a filesystem marker, retire the old marker before reporting failure and have the replacement publish its own readiness. Verify that the dependent starts again after replacement readiness. A stale marker can let the readiness probe succeed before the replacement process starts.
verify-service-restart-readiness-per-gen.title: Test readiness for each service generation

verify-standalone-wasm-process-evaluatio.text:
When changing WASM evaluation of process expressions, exercise KameProgram.evaluate directly. The standalone evaluator needs the shared host tool-resolution request and portable capture default even when no CLI session is compiled. Test captured stdout, inspected exit status, a lazily evaluated definition, caller cwd, missing-tool fallback, and denial without run grants.

When running `tests/wasm/test-memory-reuse.mjs` against a freshly built module, set `KAME_WASM` to that module's path. The script selects the binary from that variable or falls back to `build/wasm/kame.wasm`. Positional arguments have no effect on binary selection.

When changing source-backed evaluation in the JavaScript API, compile with an absolute source name and test `KameProgram.evaluate` against a relative authored import. Vary the evaluation cwd independently, verify the imported module retains its own file provenance, and check that a general read of the same file is denied when compile grants only scoped source access. A separately parsed evaluation AST needs the compiled program’s lexical source origin alongside its expression diagnostic location.
verify-standalone-wasm-process-evaluatio.title: Verify process evaluation through the standalone WASM API

verify-suspended-declaration-registratio.text: When changing declaration work that can suspend on a forwarded host request, drive prepare, request, and completion separately. Check that suspension and failure leave no partial program installed. Count repeated requests during replay, and verify that an unsuccessful registration retains the observations needed for watch to recover.
verify-suspended-declaration-registratio.title: Verify declaration registration across forwarded completions

item.text: Verify both registration-time and recipe-time views of declaration-local contributions.
